section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that although the Torah begins with "Bereishis" to draw the infinite light into the world, the inner essence of that beginning is the first commandment of "Hachodesh Hazeh Lachem."
section.t: And this is what Rabbi Yitzchak said: The Torah should not have begun except from "Hachodesh Hazeh Lachem,"
for this matter is also according to the truth
(as above at the beginning of the maamar),
because the fact that the Torah begins with "Bereishis Bara,"
even though the matter of Torah is the drawing down and revelation of the Ein Sof light, which is beyond relation to worlds,
is
because the intention of Torah is to draw down the revelation of the Ein Sof light, which is beyond limitation, into the limitation of worlds,
and therefore the Torah also contains the narrative of Maaseh Bereishis, in order to draw the unlimited light of Torah also into the world and to make from it a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He.
However, in order that the revelation of the unlimited light of Torah should also be in the world as it is in reality
(outside of the Torah, so to speak),
therefore it opened with "Bereishis,"
so that the narrative of Maaseh Bereishis
(and likewise the portions after it)
precedes the portion of "Hachodesh,"
the first mitzvah with which Israel was commanded,

so that through the study of Torah and the fulfillment of mitzvos, there should be a revelation of the unlimited light of Torah also in the part of the world as it was before the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos.
And since this opening with "Bereishis" is so that the revelation of the unlimited light of Torah and mitzvos
("Hachodesh Hazeh Lachem")
should also be in the matter of "Bereishis" as it is before the portion of "Hachodesh,"
it follows
that in the innerness of matters—the beginning is with "Hachodesh Hazeh Lachem,"
for the innerness of "Bereishis"
(which is before the portion of "Hachodesh")
is "Hachodesh Hazeh Lachem."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the revelation of the unlimited light in the world through teshuvah is at the level of "Zeh," while the innerness of "Bereishis" being "Hachodesh Hazeh Lachem" is at the higher level of "Koh," which will be fully realized in the future redemption.
section.t: And it is known
that the creation of the world on the 25th of Elul was in the aspect of "Koh,"
and on the day when Adam, the first man, was created
(the first of Tishrei)
a revelation of G-dliness was made in the world,
the aspect of "Zeh."
However, the revelation that came about through Adam is incomparable to the revelation of the Giving of the Torah.
And based on this, it can be said
that this—that "Hachodesh Hazeh Lachem" is the innerness of "Bereishis Bara"—is superior to the matter that the teshuvah of man is in a manner of unlimited
(above, section 7).

For the connection of the unlimited and the limited through the fact that the teshuvah of man is above limitation is a revelation of the unlimited light of Torah and mitzvos in the world as it is at the level of "Zeh,"

and this—that "Hachodesh Hazeh Lachem" is the innerness of "Bereishis Bara"—is a revelation of the unlimited light of Torah and mitzvos in the world that was created on the 25th of Elul, as it is at the level of "Koh."
And it can be said
that this revelation will be primarily in the redemption that follows the teshuvah at the end of the time of exile.
For through the revelation of the unlimited light in the world as it is at the level of "Zeh"
(man)
through the teshuvah at the end of the time of exile,
there will afterwards be
(immediately)
the revelation of the unlimited light also in the world
as it is at the level of "Koh,"
and through this the intention of a dwelling place in the lower realms will be completed, in the lowest level beneath which there is no lower.
And also this matter is included in that in Nissan they are destined to be redeemed
[for "they are destined to be redeemed" refers to the redemption that follows the teshuvah],
that also the revelation in the world that will be in the redemption
(through the teshuvah of Israel beforehand)
will be in the aspect of Nissan,
the unlimited light that is beyond relation to worlds.
And the revelation will be in a manner that this will be the innerness of the world itself,
in the true and complete redemption through our righteous Moshiach, speedily and truly.
